clue.text: Lackeys without power or wealth

indicators.note: without says the letter for power is dropped from the word for lackeys

parts.note: poodles are servile followers, fawning lackeys
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A complaint that flunkeys have neither influence nor riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is only a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal noun for a great abundance, as in a fortune of money, so a stand-in for riches.

clue.text: Raised some celeriac in a grow-bag without fertiliser

indicators.note: Raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gardener growing celeriac in a bag with no chemical feed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Raised' reads upward: CINAGRO, hidden in 'celeriac in a grow-bag', read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown without synthetic chemical fertilisers or pesticides.

clue.text: Much flatter white

indicators.note: Much here means most of the word, so its outside letters are lost and the inner run kept

explanation.surface: A flat white coffee, but more so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat white' looks like one phrase, the coffee, but 'white' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee made with plenty of steamed milk, ordered when you want a white coffee.

clue.text: Hi you in street, gimme money!

indicators.note: in puts the greeting and the letter for you between the street letters

parts.note: hello is a greeting like hi
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A street beggar's greeting and demand for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: As an imperative, the phrase is a demand to pay up, just like a mugger's gimme money.

clue.text: Horse we start to brush shows sign of neglect

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

indicators.note: start to picks the opening letter of the following word, brush

explanation.surface: A groom notes that the horse's coat, once brushed, reveals it has been left uncared for.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty spider webs in corners show a room has gone uncleaned, a classic mark of neglect.

clue.text: Clergyman took after dog

indicators.note: after puts the word for took behind the word for dog

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
ate means took, as food

explanation.surface: A vicar who took after his dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took after' looks like resembling, but 'took' and 'after' do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant parish priest in the Church of England is a clergyman.

clue.text: Humph! Is poaching egg middle-class?

indicators.note: poaching means taking in what belongs elsewhere, so the noise and is swallow the egg word

parts.note: boo is, like humph, a noise of disapproval
to egg on is to urge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sniff of disdain: is poaching an egg a bit suburban?
explanation.definitionFit: Conventional, propertied and conformist in outlook: the stereotype of middle-class values.

clue.text: Eeyore's poor sight

indicators.note: poor suggests something in a bad way, so the letters of the donkey's name are reordered

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh's gloomy donkey has bad eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sight' looks like vision but means an ugly thing to behold.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight in the sense of a mess or fright, something ugly to look at.

clue.text: A hint of green inside, like e.g. phlegm father hawked with perfect manners

parts.note: as means like
phlegm is an example of goo
da is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: inside places that letter within the word for hawked

parts.note: hawked means peddled, sold

indicators.note: hint of takes just the first letter of green

explanation.surface: A revolting scene of green phlegm hawked up, ending with impeccable behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hawked' looks like spitting, but means sold. 'A' before 'hint' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a child behaving impeccably well.

clue.text: Tourist mentioned these locations in the East End

indicators.note: mentioned signals that the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.words: these locations in the East End
parts.note: these locations are sites here, said with the dropped H of a Cockney East End accent: sites 'ere

explanation.surface: A visitor is pointed at the local landmarks in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End of London is home to the Cockney accent, which drops initial H, so 'here' becomes 'ere'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is someone who travels about viewing famous places, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Sacrifice bishop for pawn in trap, gaining turn

indicators.note: Sacrifice tells us to give up one letter in exchange for another
for marks the swap, the bishop's letter giving way to the pawn's

parts.note: a U-bend is the trap in a drain pipe that holds water against smells
B is the chess notation for bishop
P is the chess notation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess move: giving up a bishop for a pawn to spring a trap and win a tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface hides a plumbing trap. 'in' and 'gaining' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip something over or set it on end is to turn it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Catch Italian of 18 years stealing diamonds

parts.note: di is the Italian word for of

indicators.note: stealing means taking in, so the scholar and years words enclose the diamonds letter

parts.note: 18 is the across entry meaning a learned person, the opposite of an ignoramus
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
age is a span of years

explanation.surface: A long-serving Italian jewel thief.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside the word from 18, after SA.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a hidden drawback or snag, the same as a disadvantage.

clue.text: Cat in scrap

definitions.meaning: the snow leopard is also known by this name
a tiny amount, as in not an iota of sense

explanation.surface: A cat caught in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the snow leopard, a big cat; the other a small weight, hence a tiny quantity.

clue.text: Merry monk perhaps shakes off relative with a fondness for suits

parts.note: merry, slightly drunk, means lit

indicators.note: shakes off says the abbreviation for relative is removed from the monk word

parts.note: a monk is an example of a religious, a member of a religious order

explanation.surface: A jolly friar who sheds his family and likes nice clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fond of lawsuits means constantly going to court, the core sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Fitting furnishings etc round us

parts.note: decor is the furnishing and decoration of a room
O is round in shape
taken as written

explanation.surface: Interior decoration that suits us.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper and in good taste, so seemly or fitting in behaviour.

clue.text: Almost enable girl dancing to be recognised

indicators.note: dancing suggests movement, so the remaining letters are jumbled
Almost says the word enable loses one of its letters before use

explanation.surface: A permit that lets a girl dance and get noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last E of 'enable' to get ENABL, then shuffle it with GIRL. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to sound familiar, to be recognised or remembered.

clue.text: Supply fencing that hurts budget

indicators.note: fencing means surrounding, so the supply word encloses the cry of pain

parts.note: to lend is to supply on loan
ow is the cry meaning that hurts

explanation.surface: Paying for fencing that strains the household finances.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally of goods, cheap and basic, the bottom of the price range, as with economy products.

clue.text: On about 27 + 0 = 27

indicators.note: about says the onward word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: forth means on, onward, as in 'and so forth'
the clue points at 27-across, meaning in fact; it is the definition here
the figure zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A sum written as an equation, as though the clue were arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: '+' and '=' are link words. The answer is an archaic word for 'in truth'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned exclamation meaning truly or indeed, a synonym for in fact.

clue.text: Ignoramus stood in rear? No, no, no, no!

definitions.note: the clue's 'No' on each word asks for opposites: the reverse of an ignoramus is a learned scholar

indicators.note: the opposite of in is outside, so the word for stood goes around the word for rear

parts.note: the opposite of stood is sat
the opposite of rear is van, the front of an army

explanation.surface: A dunce told off for standing at the back of class.
explanation.walkthrough: The four 'no's tell you to replace each of the four words with its opposite: ignoramus, stood, in and rear become scholar, sat, outside and van. Read like that, the clue says SAT goes outside VAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The defining word is negated by the clue, so the answer is its opposite, a learned person.

clue.text: Drop or dump man in letter

indicators.note: in places the boy's name within the letter's name

parts.note: vee is the name of the letter V
Stig of the Dump is a children's novel whose hero, a cave boy, lives in a chalk pit

explanation.surface: Dropping or dumping a man by letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stig of the Dump' is a well-known British children's book by Clive King. 'or' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop as a tiny remaining trace or hint; the answer is the last trace of something.

clue.text: Second American vessel, sometimes called a dish

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
USS, United States Ship, prefixes American naval vessels
aka is 'also known as', meaning sometimes called

explanation.surface: A US cook's second pot, whatever you call it, makes a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek baked dish of aubergine and minced lamb in layers.

clue.text: Old investigators return and follow crook?

indicators.note: follow puts the reversed initials after the bend word

parts.note: a crook is a bend or arch, as in the crook of an arm

indicators.note: return says the agency initials are read backwards

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: Veteran detectives come back to tail a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal but means a curve. 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to an ancient period, so very old or antiquated.

clue.text: Mate being bloody stupid

indicators.note: stupid suggests nonsense, so the letters of the swear word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exasperated 'mate, you're bloody stupid'.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly British form of address between men, much like mate or chum.

clue.text: 22's stories about clubs and bars

parts.note: 22 refers to the down entry meaning mate; its abbreviation is OB, so 22's gives OBS

indicators.note: about says the stories word surrounds the clubs letter

parts.note: tales are stories
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A former pupil's yarns about nightclubs and pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: OB (old boy) is a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Bars as in barriers: things blocking the way are hindrances or impediments.

clue.text: Feature in newspaper is great!

indicators.note: in places the word for great inside the newspaper's initials

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
ace means excellent, great

explanation.surface: A rave review: the newspaper's feature article is excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect or side of something is one of its features.

clue.text: Fast boats

definitions.meaning: a number of ships sailing together, as a navy's

explanation.surface: Speedy craft.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is swift; the other a group of ships under one command.

clue.text: Doctor, I have an urge

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A patient confessing a compulsion to the GP.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is an innate impulse or urge, as in sex drive.

clue.text: Pick up drug called 'rebound' …

parts.note: a boom is an upturn or pick-up in trade
E is ecstasy
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: Collecting drugs from someone who phoned after a relapse.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next, which reuses 'pick up drug'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to come back on the one who started it, as a thrown curved stick returns: to backfire or rebound.

clue.text: … pick up drug inside, in fact

indicators.note: inside places the drug letter within the pick-up word

parts.note: a rally is a recovery or pick-up
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: collect drugs indoors, and that's a fact.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb of emphasis meaning truly or actually, a synonym of in fact.

clue.text: Couple entertaining European with lots of gadgets

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so the couple word takes in the European letter

parts.note: to hitch is to couple, as a trailer to a car

explanation.surface: A pair hosting a European guest in a gadget-filled home.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes technologically advanced design, full of electronic devices.
